obligations.text: Ensure that staff who operate or use AI systems have sufficient AI literacy.
Ensure that staff who operate or use AI systems have sufficient AI literacy.
Set up and maintain a risk management system for the whole lifecycle.
Train, validate and test on data sets that meet the quality criteria.
Draw up the technical documentation before placing it on the market.
Make the system record events (logs) automatically over its lifetime.
Make it transparent enough for deployers, with instructions for use.
Design it so that people can oversee it effectively while it is in use.
Achieve appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity.
Put a documented quality management system in place.
Complete the conformity assessment before placing it on the market.
Draw up the EU declaration of conformity and keep it for 10 years.
Affix the CE marking.
Register the system in the EU database before placing it on the market.
Set up and document post-market monitoring.
Report serious incidents to the market surveillance authorities.
Use the system according to the provider's instructions for use.
Assign human oversight to competent, trained people with authority.
Ensure that input data under the deployer's control is relevant and representative.
Monitor its operation and inform the provider of risks and serious incidents.
Keep the logs under the deployer's control for at least six months.
Inform the persons subject to decisions made or assisted by the system of its use.
Inform workers' representatives and the affected workers before using it.
obligations.condition: where the system is used at the workplace by an employer

obligations.text: Carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment before first use.
Register the use of the system in the EU database before putting it into use.
obligations.condition: where the deployer is a public authority or acts on its behalf

notes: Art. 113 dates Arts. 43, 47-49 and 72-73 from 2 August 2026, but they apply to systems that are high-risk under Chapter III, so they are shown with its date.

A high-risk system already on the market before that date is covered only if its design changes significantly afterwards; systems used by public authorities must comply by 2 August 2030 in any case (Art. 111(2)).

citations.quote: AI systems intended to be used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons or establish their credit score
citations.claim: The system is intended to evaluate the creditworthiness of consumers to decide on personal loan applications. This matches point 5(b). The fraud-detection exception does not apply, since the purpose is credit assessment.

citations.quote: Chapters I and II shall apply from 2 February 2025
2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III
citations.claim: The high-risk duties apply from 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems.
